#### The evolution of public spending in France from 1960 to 2024

### François Langot & Fabien Tripier

Graph 1/3

• French public debt rose from 28.5% of GDP in 1960 to 113.2% in 2024.

• This increase occurred in a context of a continuous rise in public spending, from

37% to 57% of GDP.

• Public revenues increased, but remained persistently below expenditures, resulting

in a continuous public deficit since 1975.

• The absence of a sufficiently favorable macroeconomic environment (low real interest rates, strong economic growth) has prevented the containment of debt

dynamics.

• The current level of debt is closely linked to the evolution of public expenditure across all levels of government (central, local, and social security).

• Debt servicing costs have remained stable, at around 2% of GDP.

• Employee compensation increased between 1960 and 1980, then stabilized, with a

slight decline since 1995.

• Other operating and production expenditures of public services have remained

broadly stable, at around 16% of GDP.

• The main driver of expenditure growth has been transfers, which rose from 11% to

26% of GDP between 1960 and 2024.

• Transfer expenditures are the main driver of the growth in public spending in

France.

• Since 1995, their increase has been driven primarily by higher healthcare expenditure (+2 percentage points of GDP) and age-related social protection expenditure (+2.15

percentage points of GDP).

• Other spending functions have either declined (education) or increased only modestly from initially low levels (environmental protection).
